prompt: A particle moving along a line has acceleration $a(t) = 6t - 4$ m/s$^2$. At $t = 0$ its velocity is $1$ m/s and its position is $2$ m. Find its position at $t = 2$ seconds, in meters.
hint: Two antiderivatives in a row: acceleration $\to$ velocity $\to$ position. Use an initial condition after each one.

hints.text: Two antiderivatives in a row: acceleration $\to$ velocity $\to$ position. Use an initial condition after each one.
Step two: $s(t) = \int (3t^2 - 4t + 1) \, dt = t^3 - 2t^2 + t + C_2$, and $s(0) = 2$ gives $C_2 = 2$. Now evaluate $s(2)$.

explanation: $s(2) = 2^3 - 2(2)^2 + 2 + 2 = 8 - 8 + 2 + 2 = 4$ m. Along the way it turns around twice: $v(t) = (3t - 1)(t - 1)$ is negative on $\left(\frac{1}{3}, 1\right)$, so it backs up to $s(1) = 2$ before moving forward to $4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Net change twice
steps: You still need $v(t)$ first, so the first constant $C_1 = 1$ is unavoidable — but the second one can be skipped this way.
